heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings (two uniform 256-bit words each); their chaining values CV1 = F_38(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: for every fixed variant a0, Pr[W7x in F7] = p7 = 287,309,824/2^32 exactly, and given it (W0..W6) is uniform and independent of W7 (Lemma 5.1); E16x is uniform for a good pair, so a lane passes the 8 tested bits with probability 2^-8 and the row-16 set with probability 160/2^32; the expected numbers of passing classes (0.53516 for the 8 accepted classes, 3.2110 for the 48 of this revision) and good pairs (13,152; 64,116 for the 48) per first block; independence across first blocks.
heuristics.scope: The expected counts per first block that fix the work (V_MAX), the law of the second-block words that defines q3, and the independence of the first blocks (proof.md Sections 5 and 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact distribution of the number of passing classes over all 2^32 values of A_{-1} for the 8 classes (p8hits.c, Appendix A.2); 29,360,128 (2^22 + 2^23 + 2^24) real first blocks through the attack's own filters with the 8 classes (proof.md Section 13.1, e2ep8.c): passing classes, good pairs and stage-3a passes within 0.07% of their expectations, 14,199 row-16 passes against 14,385.0 expected (z = -1.55), every one checked exactly in Python (the first block gives the chaining value, the variant is selected, rows -4..16 hold in both members); the organizer experiment a0-online-r38. The 48-class revision (Appendix D) applies the same per-variant law to 48 H-closed classes; Section D.7 measures q3 per class and finds no class dependence, and the ledger charges Pr[some class passes] as 1 on every block, so no exact class-pass distribution is used (Section D.8).
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem; tested on 2^24 first blocks, not 2^82. The class tests of one first block are correlated (at most 2 of the 32 maximal classes pass); only the expectations and the exact probability that some class passes enter the ledger.

heuristics.statement: For a good pair, q3 = the average over the 958,464 selected variants (the 48 H-closed classes of Appendix D.4; the 196,608 variants of the accepted 8-class set are a subset and the same q3_model is used) of Pr[the pair is in the accepted event: rows 16..21 of both members follow every cell, '+' pair and two-bit condition of P8 closing at rows 16..21, row 19 on its signed differences only, the relation E18 = E17 (bits 24, 23, 15) not imposed, and the state words A34..A37, E34..E37 of the two members are equal]; q3 >= q3_model = 2^-95.8752.
heuristics.scope: The expected number of successes E[X] = N_FB g q3 and hence N_FB (proof.md Sections 7 and 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Our preregistered measurements: (1) the printed-cell event (proof.md Section 7.4 and Appendix A.9; preregistration hashed before the first seed): traillab, 32 fresh seeds x 2^28 window samples on real compressions with the real message expansion, row 16 exact (the 160-word set), W8 drawn from the 196,608 selected variants, W6 uniform, W7 uniform in F7, the accepted event counted (prefix rows 16..21 times zero output difference): mean 2^-96.3251, seed sd 0.577, declared one-sided 99% Student lower bound 2^-96.5755, halves -96.314 / -96.337, every diagnostic 0; (2) the ratio of this event (E18 = E17 not imposed) to it (proof.md Section 7.5 and Appendix A.11; preregistered before the first seed): traillab shared-carrier window, 400 fresh seeds x 2^24 samples, both events counted on the same samples, ratio 1.420 (0.5054 bit), jackknife SE 0.0387, declared one-sided 99% lower bound 0.4149 bit; (3) a second lower bound of the same printed-cell event from the shipped replica (proof.md Section 7.4b and Appendix A.12; preregistered before the first seed, SHA-256 12cadbfa...): 2,000 fresh replicates of smc_replicate, 100 pools of 20, 0 failed rebuilds, L = -96.2499, pool sd 0.1699, declared one-sided 99% lower bound 2^-96.2901 (and 2^-96.2893 by a percentile bootstrap over the 100 pools); q3_model = max(2^-96.5755, 2^-96.2901) x 2^0.4149 = 2^-96.2901 x 2^0.4149 = 2^-95.8752. Our replica (an independent implementation, Section 7.3): 960 calibration replicates, mean 2^-96.3095, every success rebuilt into a verified 38-step semi-free-start collision and accepted by the counted program; the organizer experiment a0-q3-r38 runs it with a pass rule frozen before its calibration (pooled mean of 20 >= 2^-97.0). 1a695f0b's estimator for its event (quoted): mean 2^-96.3683 over 20 runs. No transfer between classes or events is used. (4) the per-class measurement of this revision (Appendix D.7; q3cls.py forces the shipped replica's class draw one class at a time): 200 replicates for each of the 48 classes, 9,600 replicates on disjoint seeds, 0 failed rebuilds, 65,945 rebuilt and accepted semi-free-start pairs; pooled log2 q3 = -96.2725, per-class means min -96.5648, max -96.3523, sd 0.0506 against a mean SEM 0.0560, chi-square for a common q3 40.2 on 47 degrees of freedom (p ~ 0.75), so the classes are exchangeable at the 0.05-bit level and applying q3_model to all 958,464 variants adds no unmeasured class dependence. The organizer experiment a0-q3-r38 now draws its variant uniformly from all 958,464 variants, i.e. it measures the pooled quantity the ledger uses.
heuristics.limitations: A maximum of two Monte-Carlo lower bounds for the printed-cell factor (one from our own tool, which is not shipped because of the 65,536-byte source limit, one from the shipped replica) times one for the ratio (confidence at least 97% by the union bound); the replica and 1a695f0b's estimator are other implementations whose means agree with it within 0.05 bit. The ratio comes from a few lineage clusters per seed; H3 and the replica do not cover the extra pairs (E18 different from E17). The replica estimates a lower bound (E18 = E17 as printed, row-19 proposals from 1a695f0b's twelve conditions, W23 in F23, the characteristic's path from row 22). The bound treats the 32 seeds as independent replicates (the seed is the cluster); the mean of per-seed log2 values is conservative for log2 q3 (Jensen). The class-independence of q3 rests on the per-class measurement of Section D.7 (9,600 replicates, 0.05-bit resolution); its 0.73-bit distance from the pass rule 2^-97.0 and 0.40-bit distance from q3_model are larger than that resolution.

heuristics.statement: Let R_f be the number of selected variants of first block f that are good and pass row 16, and A_t the event that trial t = (f, a0) succeeds. Averaged over successes, the other variants of the same first block pass row 16 at most 2^-7.5 times: sum_t Pr[A_t] E[R_f - 1 | A_t] <= 2^-7.5 E[X_f].
heuristics.scope: The per-first-block Bonferroni bound Pr[X_f >= 1] >= E[X_f] - E[X_f (X_f - 1)]/2 >= (1 - 2^-8.5) E[X_f] (proof.md Section 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Under H1 the law of (CV1, a0) given a success is the law of the successes of the Step-3 sampler (proof.md Section 13.5). Our measurement on successes of the accepted event: 12,028 successes of 8 independent runs of the replica's sampler (all 8 classes, a0 uniform on the 196,608 variants), each rebuilt into a verified pair and accepted by step3b, every selected variant of every passing class of its chaining value tested: 32 other row-16 passes against 21.95 under independence, 2^-8.55 per success, one-sided 99% upper bounds 2^-7.97 (Poisson) and 2^-7.79 (Student over the 8 runs), below the premise; the stage-3a passes of the other variants are at 1.0008 of their expectation. 1a695f0b measured 2 other row-16 passes on 750 successes (quoted).
heuristics.limitations: The successes are sampled by the replica's sampler, a sub-event of the accepted event (row-19 relation sets, W23 in F23, zero differences from row 22), not real collisions; successes within a run share ancestors (the Student bound uses the 8 independent runs). The other row-16 passes exceed independence by a factor 1.46 (z = +2.15); the premise counts row-16 passes only, which is conservative. No organizer execution.

heuristics.statement: The total computation spent to obtain the characteristic P8 of 1a695f0b (its signed-difference SAT sweep, coupling checks and estimators; failed and repeated runs included) is at most A_C = 2^56 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger: A_C = 2^56 is 12.4 bits above P8's own published search bound of 2^43.61 units; it enters the claimed time and preprocessing (57.58496).
heuristics.extrapolation: P8's search is published with its run log (1a695f0b Section 3.2, quoted; participant-run): 38 solver runs of at most 10,800 s (230,183 s in all), P8 found in 4,714 s with a 662-s coupling check; its author bounds the search, S, the class data and all development by one 10-core machine for less than 2^21 core-seconds, which at our measured 3,797,484 SHA-256 compressions per second is 2^43.61 units, 12.4 bits under A_C = 2^56. Our own measurements of the same kind of search (proof.md Appendix C, from fb176310): a 39-step characteristic derived from scratch with the public tool of [LLW24] in 2^36.04 units; published figures up to 2^39.15 units, 16.85 bits under A_C. A_C = 2^56 leaves at least 12.4 bits over P8's own search for unrecorded failed and repeated runs; it replaces fb176310's inherited 2^78.
heuristics.limitations: An allowance, not our measurement: we did not rerun P8's search; its log and the 2^21 core-second bound are the author's. With A_C = 2^84 the claim would be 85.99046.

heuristics.statement: S (the dense part of P8's semi-free-start pair) and the 8 class descriptors with their product description are obtained at a total cost of at most A_S = 2^56 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (A_S = 2^56, well below 0.001% of T); it is more than 20 bits above the 662-s coupling check.
heuristics.extrapolation: 1a695f0b obtained the pair in its 662-s coupling check and the class descriptors by 32 passes over a hash of c7 (quoted); our exhaustive pass over all 2^32 values of a0 (p8fam.c, 102 s, 69 MB peak) reproduces the 8 classes and their 24,576 members each, and selftest checks the product description. A_S = 2^56 is more than 20 bits above the 662-s coupling check and replaces fb176310's inherited 2^74.
heuristics.limitations: An allowance: the pair search was run by 1a695f0b, not by us; its memory (2^28.094, measured by its author) sets the claimed peak (H6).

heuristics.statement: All development of this package (exhaustive passes, end-to-end runs, the q3 runs, the replica's development and calibration, the H3 measurement, the program scans and the cloud checks of the hoisted programs; failed trials and reruns included) is at most DEV = 2^56 target compressions. H4c is a time charge; the memory figure is H6.
heuristics.scope: The development item of the ledger (DEV = 2^56, well below 0.001% of T).
heuristics.extrapolation: Recorded development below 1.5 x 10^5 CPU-seconds (proof.md Section 13.4); at 10^10 word operations per CPU-second that is below 2^51 operations = 2^39.3 compressions, so 2^56 is more than 2^16 times the recorded work. Every development execution whose output the claim uses ran under a hard address-space cap of 2^27 or 2^28 bytes with its peak measured by memmeter (the shared-carrier runs of proof.md Section 7.5 by /usr/bin/time -v, at most 2^27.74 bytes), at most 2^27.77 bytes (proof.md Section 14 (c2), Appendix A.10).
heuristics.limitations: Accounting of our own runs, not an organizer log; declared here because the review of fb176310 recorded it as an implicit heuristic (H-implicit-development-bound). There are no other development executions in this construction.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5, a straight-line word-RAM program that evaluates E16x = C16 + W0 + s0(W1) and its stage-3a test for 256 variants at once (bit L of every 256-bit word belongs to variant L) is charged its instruction list: every load, store and spill is counted, 64 registers, complements are free except in a mixed and/or (one more operation), no fused AND-NOT; one stage-2 program per batch, with the batch's constant bits of a0 folded into it, and one stage-1 program per (class, G1) whose stored planes the 32 stage-2 programs of its y values load (each store and each load is an instruction and is counted); no target compression is evaluated this way.
heuristics.scope: The plane-program term of the ledger (37,290.96 of the 43,396.40 data-dependent operations per first block).
heuristics.extrapolation: The 24 stage-1 and 768 stage-2 programs are generated and counted by experiments/a0hoist38.py (build_e16, group, Prog.schedule, run_prog): 574 to 579 instructions per stage-1 program and 681 to 725 per stage-2 program (mean 701.65), spills of at most 10 slots; every stage-2 program is executed with its stage-1 program by the organizer experiment a0-online-r38 on all its 256 lanes and compared with the scalar definition (196,608 lanes per request in the local emulation, 0 mismatches), as are the batches of the passing classes of its trials 0..5 and 6 sampled batches in selftest; on the cloud 23,592,960 lanes of 120 random chaining values, 0 mismatches.
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited; the same reading was accepted for fb176310 and 2d1c4fc2. Program generation is charged 2^32 operations per program, not counted instruction by instruction. With a scalar evaluation (38 operations per variant) the claim would be 89.42650.

heuristics.statement: The peak memory is the maximum over the counted phases, <= 2^28.1 bytes (claim memory_log2_bytes = 28.1). The counted phases are the online program (86,428,192 bytes = 2^26.3650: the code of the 144 stage-1 and 3,744 stage-2 programs at 32 bytes per instruction, the hoisted planes, the tables, planes, the 4,656-word class table and state), the 2,000-replicate H2 run of the shipped replica (executed one replicate at a time in one process: peak RSS 21,264 KiB = 2^24.38 bytes), the computations behind the advice (the largest is the Step-1 solve of P8, measured by its author at 279,720 KB = 2^28.094 bytes) and the development executions (run under address-space caps of 2^27 and 2^28 bytes, measured peaks at most 2^27.77 bytes).
heuristics.scope: The memory metric of the claim and the score 85.13695 + (28.1 - 20) = 93.23695.
heuristics.extrapolation: proof.md Section 14 lists every online component; the computations behind P8 measured by 1a695f0b (Step-1 solve 2^28.094, signed search at most 2^27.92, class descriptors 2^25.14; single-threaded, sequential, quoted); our solver instances (fb176310: 2^26.82 to 2^27.56); our development executions measured with /usr/bin/time -v (largest: the trail tool at 4 threads, 2^27.48) and run under prlimit --as caps with memmeter (Section 14 (c2), Appendix A.10); the organizer experiments run within the 128 MiB sandbox (66 MB and 27 MB peaks under Linux). The 48-class program's two organizer requests were emulated locally with the organizer request shape and limits (Appendix D.6): the online experiment returned its 14 pairs in 4.7 s at a 45 MiB peak, the q3 experiment its 21 pairs in 3.4 s at 23 MiB, both inside 20 s and 128 MiB.
heuristics.limitations: The 2^28.094 figure is the author's sampled measurement (every 0.2 s), not ours; the machine model defines no code size (32 bytes per instruction is the generous choice).

heuristics.statement: In the hoisting step, two Boolean DAG nodes of the 32 batch programs with equal 512-bit evaluation signatures compute the same function (no false equivalence), so merging them leaves the generated program equal to the unhoisted one.
heuristics.scope: The node merging of the hoisted plane program (proof.md Section 9, hoisting): whether the generated program computes the reference row-16 filter. The counted operations are those of the generated program as written, exact whatever it computes; a false merge could only change which pairs pass the filter, hence the success probability, and every output is verified with the target.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our theory. The generated program agrees bit for bit with the reference on 23,592,960 cloud lanes (0 disagreements) and the organizer experiment a0-online-r38 (196,608 lanes, 0 mismatches); a false merge would change outputs on a positive fraction of inputs.
heuristics.limitations: Our theory, not a theorem: equal 512-bit evaluation signatures are taken to mean equal functions. Checked on 23,592,960 cloud lanes and the organizer's 196,608 lanes with 0 disagreements, not on all inputs.

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is a verified collision of the target (Lemma 6.1, proof.md Section 6.1).

Algorithm: the two-block attack of ePrint 2026/1120 with the characteristic P8 of dariolina's 1a695f0b (its cells, its semi-free-start pair, the Step-1 solution S; member x = M) and the A0-variant method of fb176310 and 2d1c4fc2, with the class set of Appendix D.4: 48 H-closed c7 classes (958,464 variants; 12 each of 24,576, 21,504, 18,432 and 15,360 members), each a union of 3 G1 groups of batches of 256 lanes. One W7 test decides a class and every variant of a passing class is a good pair; per (class, G1) one stage-1 program computes the y-independent planes and 3,744 straight-line stage-2 batch programs fold the batch constants, evaluate E16x for 256 variants and test the 8 lowest bits shared by the 160 row-16 words; passing lanes resolved in scalar form; a row-16 pass checked through row 21 (row 19 on its signed differences only, E18 = E17 not imposed); rows 22..37 computed untested and both outputs compared (proof.md Section 6.1).

Cost: fixed caps. N_FB = 561,737,269,563,571,647,185,252 first blocks (2^78.89424), each one target compression plus 35 counted operations, and V_MAX = 114,490,695,561,031,602,664,415,012,614 counted data-dependent operations (halt when exceeded, tested at the start of every block and after every class; at most V_MAX + 352,668, Appendix D.8); allowances A_C = A_S = DEV = 2^56 (H4a, H4b, H4c); counted precomputation 2^43.925; final verification. Counted program experiments/a0hoist38.py: 144 stage-1 programs of 568..593 instructions, 3,744 stage-2 programs of 675..727 (2,694,240 instructions), 2,825 operations for a row-16 pass. Exact total 2^85.1369435390 (Appendix D.8), claimed 85.13695.

Success probability at least 0.39 (the bound is exactly 0.39) under H1 (independent uniform first-block chaining values), H2 (q3 >= 2^-95.8752 for the accepted event, unchanged from the accepted filing: max(2^-96.5755, 2^-96.2901) x 2^0.4149), H3 (averaged over successes the other variants of the same first block pass row 16 at most 2^-7.5 times; measured 2^-8.55) and Chebyshev caps. The 48-class set applies that q3 to 958,464 variants; it was measured on every class (200 replicates each, 9,600 replicates, pooled 2^-96.2725, class means sd 0.0506 against a mean SEM 0.0560, chi-square 40.2/47, Appendix D.7), 0.73 bit above the pass rule 2^-97.0 and 0.40 bit above q3_model. Pr[some class passes] is charged as 1 per block (conservative, Section D.8).

Memory: peak 2^28.1 bytes = maximum over the counted phases: online 86,428,192 bytes = 2^26.3650 (Appendix D.8), preprocessing: the Step-1 solve of P8 measured by its author at 279,720 KB = 2^28.094 bytes, the development executions under 2^27 and 2^28 address-space caps (Appendix A.10). Nonuniform advice: 48 class descriptors and their 4,608 batch constants, 4,656 words = 18,624 bytes < 2^14 (declared 14). The online figure is 1.73 bits below the Step-1 peak that sets the claim.
